images.caption: Beach at Ferryside. View towards Ferry Point. As the names suggest, this was an historically important crossing place on the Towy estuary. It was on the medieval pilgrims' route to St. David's cathedral. After the railway opened in 1852, holidaymakers used to arrive by train at Ferryside and cross by boat to Llansteffan. Ferries no longer operate from here, but we don't know when they stopped.
images.alt: Beach at Ferryside. View towards Ferry Point. As the names suggest, this was an historically important crossing place on the Towy estuary. images.filename: Ferryside, view after a Bang^ - geograph.org.uk - 1179299.jpg
images.caption:
Ferryside: view after a Bang! As I moseyed along the beach, I suddenly heard a big bang and turned round to this view across the Towy estuary  there is a military test firing area at Ginst Point (at SN3208), where the explosion took place.
A second bang occurred a minute or so later.

Pumsaint Coronation Hall
